forks.question: Which isolation contract should #621 establish? The issue offers two approaches with different write permissions and per-invocation costs, while the current tests pin one writable root container per part. Either choice must protect later acceptance from earlier commands and selectors, preserve captured policy, private staging, shared allowances and cleanup ownership, add daemon-free and opt-in real Go/pytest attack tests, and report cost against the current implementation.

options.says: Run each acceptance invocation, including its discovery and helper compilation, in a fresh container from the immutable prepared image and pristine staged inputs, allowing writes inside that disposable container but carrying no workload-modified files or caches into later invocations; pay container startup, staging and cold-cache costs for each invocation.

Retain a container per part, but run workloads as an unprivileged user over a read-only runtime and dependency image, give each invocation private writable inputs and scratch, and compile helpers with a fresh protected build cache; reject writes outside that scratch and avoid restarting the container for each invocation.

usage.summary: Wrote [proposal.json](/var/folders/fz/s3p17rl97r30y73d180fjbmc0000gn/T/invariant-plan-3598311910/proposal.json) asking whether to use fresh containers or unprivileged execution over a read-only image. This choice affects write permissions and invocation cost; `repo/` remains unchanged.
